title: Group-scoped chats + cross-project tool access within groups
description:
Enable a single chat to operate over a set of projects (a group scope) and safely call tools against any project in that group.

Key capabilities:
- New chat contexts for group scope stored under `/.factory/chats/groups/<groupId>/...`.
- ChatsTools prompt/settings plumbing for group contexts, including listing member projects in the system prompt.
- Tool-call routing that can target a chosen project via `projectId` argument.
- Central enforcement in `factoryToolsManager.executeTool` so tool calls can only target projects within the chat’s allowed group scope.

Domain clarification:
- Use a single `ProjectsGroup` entity for all groupings.
- Add `ProjectsGroup.type: 'MAIN' | 'SCOPE'` to distinguish cohesive/main vs loose/scope groupings.
- Group membership is derived from `Project.scopeGroupIds` (a project is in a group iff `scopeGroupIds` includes `groupId`).

features.title: Add group chat contexts and persistence under /.factory/chats/groups/<groupId>/
features.description:
## Goal
Introduce group-scoped chat contexts and store/load them from a dedicated folder.

## Scope
- Add new `ChatContextType` values for group chats (name TBD but likely `GROUP` / `GROUP_TOPIC`).
- Extend `ChatContext` to carry `groupId`.
- Persist group chats under `/.factory/chats/groups/<groupId>/...`.
- Update context <-> path mapping so:
  - `getChatContextPath(...)` produces the group path
  - `getChatContextFromFilename(...)` parses group paths correctly
- Ensure `ChatsTools.subscribe()` emits add/change/delete updates for group chat files.

## Acceptance criteria
- Can create and load a chat whose context includes `{ type: GROUP, groupId }`.
- Group chat files are written under `/.factory/chats/groups/<groupId>/`.
- Parsing round-trip holds:
  - `context -> path -> context` yields the same `type/groupId`.
- Existing project/general chat paths continue to work unchanged.

## Implementation notes
Likely changes:
- `src/chats/chatsTypes.ts`
- `src/chats/chatsUtils.ts`
- `src/chats/chatsConstants.ts` (constants for folder name)
- `src/constants.ts` (if shared constants are used for chats roots)

features.title: Group prompt plumbing in ChatsTools (member projects list + projectId tool-call guidance)
features.description:
## Goal
When a chat is group-scoped, ChatsTools must generate the correct system prompt and settings for that scope, including:
- what the group is
- which projects are in scope
- how the assistant should target a specific project when calling tools

## Scope
- Add default settings + default system prompt for group contexts in `chatsConstants`.
- Extend `getDefaultChatPrompt` / `getDefaultChatSettings` handling for group contexts.
- Extend `ChatsTools.getSettingsPrompt`, `updateChatSettings`, `updateCompletionSettings` switches to support group context.
- Add a group context renderer that resolves:
  - group metadata (including `ProjectsGroup.type`)
  - list of member projects (id + title + description if available)
- Membership resolution must be derived from Project specs:
  - a project is in group iff `Project.scopeGroupIds` contains `groupId`
- Prompt must explicitly instruct:
  - For project-dependent tools, include `projectId` in tool arguments.
  - Valid `projectId`s are limited to those in the group.

## Acceptance criteria
- For `{ type: GROUP, groupId }` contexts, `ChatsTools.getSettingsPrompt` includes group.type + member project list.
- For non-group contexts, existing prompts are unchanged.
- The group prompt explicitly teaches the model to add `projectId` for project-dependent tool calls.

## Implementation notes
- ChatsTools is instantiated once for a multi-project organiser, so it should not be hard-bound to a single project.
- Prefer injecting resolvers/providers into ChatsTools creation (e.g. `resolveGroup(groupId)` and `resolveGroupProjectIds(groupId)` and `resolveProject(projectId)` callbacks) rather than importing concrete tools directly.
- Likely changes:
  - `src/chats/chatsConstants.ts`
  - `src/chats/chatsUtils.ts`
  - `src/chats/ChatsTools.ts`
  - `src/project/*` and `src/projectsgroups/*` if a new resolver surface is needed.

features.title: Tool-call projectId injection + missing-projectId retry behavior
features.description:
## Goal
Make it easy and reliable for the LLM to target the correct project when calling tools.

## Scope
- Extend the tool-call wrapper (client-side `callTool`) to inject `projectId` similarly to existing `storyId`/`featureId` injection.
- Rules:
  - If chat context is project-descendant (has `chatContext.projectId`) and args do not include `projectId`, inject it.
  - If chat context is group-scoped (has `groupId` but no single `projectId`), then for project-dependent tool calls:
    - require `projectId` in args, OR
    - return a structured error that instructs the model to retry with `projectId`.
- Define ‘project-dependent tool’ classification:
  - Prefer tool schema metadata (e.g. tool declares it requires a project scope), otherwise maintain a conservative allowlist.

## Acceptance criteria
- In project-scoped chats, tool calls succeed without explicitly providing `projectId`.
- In group-scoped chats, tool calls either:
  - include `projectId` and execute against that project, or
  - fail with a clear retry message instructing to include `projectId`.
- Tests cover injection and missing-projectId behavior.

## Implementation notes
- Client wrapper currently calls `factoryToolsManager.executeTool(projectId, name, args)`; update to route using `args.projectId ?? chatContext.projectId`.
- Ensure enforcement is still centralized (Feature: executeTool enforcement).

features.title: Central scope enforcement in factoryToolsManager.executeTool (allow only group-member projects)
features.description:
## Goal
Enforce group scope at the single source of truth: `factoryToolsManager.executeTool`.

## Scope
- Extend `executeTool` to accept an optional execution scope (preferred: pass `chatContext` or `{ scopeType, groupId }`).
- When scope is group-scoped:
  - determine allowed projectIds for the group by reading project specs
  - a project is allowed iff `Project.scopeGroupIds` contains `groupId`
  - reject calls where the routed `projectId` is not in the allowed set
- Ensure rejection error is deterministic and model-actionable (so the agent can retry with a correct `projectId`).

## Acceptance criteria
- Tool execution succeeds for a projectId that is a member of the group (by `scopeGroupIds` membership).
- Tool execution fails (with clear error) for a projectId outside the group.
- Tool execution behavior for non-group chats is unchanged.
- Tests cover allow/deny scenarios and ensure no bypass through missing/incorrect scope.

## Implementation notes
- Prefer passing scope into `executeTool` rather than re-resolving it indirectly.
- The enforcement should run before dispatching to the underlying per-project toolset.
- Likely changes:
  - `factoryToolsManager` implementation (not yet in context files)
  - membership resolver helper (Feature 5)
  - client wrapper / orchestrator call sites to pass scope
  - tests for the manager

features.title: Group typing + project membership: ProjectsGroup.type enum + Project.scopeGroupIds (+ membership helpers)
features.description:
## Goal
Make group semantics explicit while keeping a single group entity:
- all groupings are `ProjectsGroup`
- `ProjectsGroup.type` distinguishes cohesive/main vs loose/scope
- membership is derived solely from `Project.scopeGroupIds`

## Scope
- Extend `ProjectsGroup` to include a `type` enum (exact values TBD; e.g. `MAIN | SCOPE`).
- Extend Project spec/types to include:
  - `scopeGroupIds?: string[]`
- Define membership rule used across the system:
  - a project is in group iff `Project.scopeGroupIds` contains `groupId`
- Provide helper APIs to resolve membership used by:
  - ChatsTools prompt rendering (group -> member projects)
  - `factoryToolsManager.executeTool` enforcement (is target project allowed for group?)

## Acceptance criteria
- A group has a `type` field that clients can use to distinguish ‘main’ vs ‘scope’ intent.
- A project can belong to many groups via `scopeGroupIds`.
- Membership resolution function can return all projectIds for a groupId by scanning project specs.
- Tests cover:
  - group type parsing/validation
  - membership resolution correctness

## Implementation notes
- Likely changes:
  - `src/projectsgroups/projectsGroupsTypes.ts` (add `type`)
  - `src/projectsgroups/ProjectsGroupsTools.ts` (create/edit validation for `type`)
  - `src/project/projectTypes.ts` (ProjectSpec: add `scopeGroupIds`)
  - `src/project/ProjectTools.ts` (create/update project spec validation)
  - Add a helper module for membership resolution (e.g. `src/projectsgroups/groupsMembership.ts`).
- Avoid duplicating membership in `projects_groups.json` to prevent drift; membership should come from Project specs.
